s.g: One of the long benches in a church, seating several persons, usually fixed to the floor and facing the chancel.
s.x: In many churches some pews are reserved for either clerical or liturgical officials such as canons, or for prominent families.

s.g: (by extension, in the plural) The congregation of a church.
An enclosed compartment in a church which provides seating for a group of people, often a prominent family.
Any structure shaped like a church pew, such as a stall, formerly used by money lenders, etc.; a box in a theatre; or a pen or sheepfold.
An expression of disgust in response to an unpleasant odor.
(childish) Representative of the sound made by the firing of a gun, particularly a blaster in science fiction.

pew.f: Initialism of pink-eyed white (mouse or rat).

s.g: (countable) Any of various tyrant flycatchers of the genus Contopus.
(uncountable) An American version of the children's game gilli-danda.

pews.f: third-person singular simple present indicative of pew

s.g: An alloy of approximately 93–98% tin and 1–2% copper, and the balance of antimony.
(historical) An alloy of tin and lead.
A beer tankard made from pewter.
A dark, dull grey colour, like that of the metal.
Of a dark, dull grey colour, like that of the metal.
